name: the allergy review again, after the owner chose 'Both'
source: test review 08 with the owner's choice

review.text: Told the waiter about my nut allergy and still had a reaction after the chicken tikka. Ended up using my EpiPen. Not acceptable.

fields.name: Ember & Spice Grill
fields.tone_notes: Warm, friendly and family-run. We talk to customers like regulars, even on their first visit. Short, upbeat sentences with a little East London charm. Use the customer's first name. Never pushy or salesy. Always say thank you. On bad reviews: apologise sincerely, never argue, and invite them back to make it right.
fields.halal_statement: All our meat is halal, certified by HMC.
fields.allergen_statement: Our kitchen handles nuts, sesame, gluten and dairy. Please tell our team about any allergy before you order.
recovery_offers: A free dessert on your next visit

owner_choice.question: This review mentions an allergic reaction. Do you want to reply publicly, contact them privately, or both?

content.text: Hannah, thank you for telling us, and we are so sorry you had such a frightening experience. We take this very seriously, and we are glad you are able to share it with us. Our team will be in touch with you directly, and you are also welcome to reach us at hello@emberandspice.co.uk or on +44 20 7946 0123 whenever suits you. The Ember & Spice Grill family

checks.reason: Warm, sincere apology, uses first name and thanks her. It rightly drops the upbeat, charming style for a serious allergy complaint.
Gives the restaurant's real email and phone and promises direct follow-up. It stays careful rather than detailed, which suits the situation.
English, matching the review. Plain words.
Opening differs from the last replies. The closing sign-off matches reply 1, but the maker's rules require the profile sign-off name, so this is acceptable.
No em-dashes, emojis, hashtags or banned words.

The email and phone match the profile. Passing to the team is backed by the owner's recorded choice to reply publicly and contact privately. 'Frightening' is a mild, reasonable reading of a review that mentions an EpiPen.
Only number is the phone number, which matches the profile exactly.
'Hannah' matches reviewer 'Hannah P.'. The sign-off matches the profile.
No claim about the cause of the reaction. The reply neither admits fault nor denies it.
No food, halal, allergen or ingredient claims made.
No targeting or wording based on personal traits.
Nothing offered in exchange for a review or for changing it.
Does not repeat the allergy, the dish or any order details publicly. Uses only what she wrote and the restaurant's own contact details.
No medical, legal or financial advice, and no compensation offered.
Phone numbers and emails are fine in Google review replies.

The maker's rules say to escalate allergic-reaction reviews, but the owner has already chosen to reply publicly and contact privately, so drafting is allowed. The reply has no refund, no offer, no argument, no staff names and no em-dashes, and it uses the correct sign-off.
